page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, provisioned with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz (4.0 GB per vCPU) and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. Unlike standard m6i instances, the m6idn includes 237 GB of dedicated local NVMe SSD instance storage. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI, along with AES and SHA-NI cryptographic support. No discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results show balanced single-core throughput alongside core-count-constrained parallel performance. Geekbench recorded a single-core score of 1601.0 (average) and a multi-core score of 3388.0 (weak). Similarly, stress-ng demonstrated average single-core performance at 1892.08, but fell into the bottom 25% for multi-core compute at 3862.58. The instance demonstrates solid data compression throughput, achieving 28.23 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip tests and 10.34 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, though multi-threaded bzip3 fell into the bottom 10% (19.62 GB/sec). Memory throughput on large blocks reached 30.03 GB/sec for reads and 25.36 GB/sec for writes.

Network and web delivery show stable mid-tier metrics, with static web serving throughput hitting 6.34 GB/sec. In-memory operations yielded 3.96 million operations/sec for Redis SET workloads, while PassMark database operations scored 1979.81. Inference tests with small 135M language models delivered 379.86 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 107.44 tokens/sec for text generation, supported by AVX-512 VNNI vector execution.

From an efficiency standpoint, the m6idn.xlarge is designed for scenarios that need a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory balance augmented by fast, local NVMe storage without relying solely on network-attached EBS volumes. Given its 4-vCPU ceiling, it is best suited for small-to-medium databases, caching layers, log processing, CI/CD runners, and web application servers requiring low-latency scratch disk space.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine operating on the Nitro System, featuring a 4-vCPU, 2-core Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 237 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps without discrete GPUs. Benchmarks exhibit consistent single-threaded execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1601.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 28.23 GB/sec, while multi-core compute is limited by the 4-vCPU layout. Memory bandwidth reaches 30.03 GB/sec for large reads, paired with 6.34 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Offering direct local high-speed disk alongside AVX-512 vector support, the m6idn.xlarge is well-suited for transactional databases, microservices, caching nodes, and CI/CD pipelines requiring rapid local IOPS.
